title: Erdős #205: Powers of 2 plus numbers with few prime factors

problemStatement.formal: \exists^\infty n,\, \forall k\, (2^k < n \Rightarrow \Omega(n - 2^k) \geq c\sqrt{\log n/\log\log n})
problemStatement.plain: Is it true that all sufficiently large n can be written as 2^k + m where Omega(m) < log log m? NO - disproved by Barreto-Leeham (2026).
whyMatters: Connects powers of 2 with prime factor counting
Related to Romanoff's theorem on 2^k + p
Uses covering systems, a key tool in combinatorial number theory
First Erdős problem disproved via AI-assisted proof (2026)

proven: bigOmega_one/prime/prime_pow/mul: all Ω properties PROVED from Mathlib
De Polignac number verification: 127 and 149 (all remainders composite)
Orders of 2 mod primes: verified for {3, 5, 7, 13, 17, 241}
knownResults.goal: All tractable results proved. 6 axioms remain (deep analytic/number-theoretic results).

currentState.focus: Eliminated 3 axioms (bigOmega_prime_pow, bigOmega_mul, remainder_achieves_min). Added concrete computations and covering system formalization.
currentState.activeApproach: Axiom reduction via Mathlib primeFactorsList API + Finset.inf'
currentState.nextAction: Problem is complete. Remaining 6 axioms are deep published results not in Mathlib.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Eliminated 3 axioms (9→6) by proving bigOmega_prime_pow from Nat.primeFactorsList_prime_pow, bigOmega_mul from Nat.perm_primeFactorsList_mul, and remainder_achieves_min from Finset.inf'_le. Added 12 concrete Ω computations, covering system formalization with de Polignac number verification (127, 149), and orders of 2 mod primes.
builtItems: bigOmega_mul: Ω(ab) = Ω(a) + Ω(b) (proved from Nat.perm_primeFactorsList_mul)
remainder_achieves_min: Finset.inf' lower bound (proved from Finset.inf'_le)
loglog_mono_nat: log log monotonicity (proved from Real.log_le_log)
12 concrete Ω values: Ω(2)=1 through Ω(30030)=6
insights: Nat.primeFactorsList_prime_pow exists in current Mathlib - directly gives Ω(p^k) = k
Nat.perm_primeFactorsList_mul gives List.Perm, then .length_eq converts to length equality
Nat.log_le_of_le_pow is the key lemma for showing k ∈ Finset.range(log₂n + 1)
Finset.inf'_le directly proves the minimum is a lower bound for any element
The covering system {3,5,7,13,17,241} uses orders {2,4,3,12,8,24} with lcm=24
127 is the smallest de Polignac number (verified: all 7 remainders composite)
mathlibGaps: No covering system theory in Mathlib
